lines.en: of the conjunction of the planets with the two nodes of the Moon) It should not remain hidden from the seekers of this art that among the astrologers regarding

lines.en: the beneficence and maleficence of the Head and Tail [of the Dragon], there is much disagreement. The majority are of the opinion that the Head is absolutely benefic

lines.text: و ذنب نحس و بعضی هر دو را نحس دانند غایتش انکه ذنب نحس است و بعضی دیگر گویند که

lines.text: چون سعد مقارن راس شود سعد بود و چون نحس مقارن او شود نحس و ذنب بخلاف
lines.en: when a benefic is conjoined with the Head, it is benefic, and when a malefic is conjoined with it, it is malefic, and the Tail is the opposite

lines.en: of this, meaning when a benefic is conjoined with it, it is malefic, and when a malefic is conjoined with it, it is benefic.

lines.en: And this one couplet of Sheikh Nizami supports this statement: (From the omen, your enemy's turn will return, like Mars

lines.text: و معلم اول ارسطاطالیس گوید راس الجوزهر مع سایر الکواکب یقویها و یزید فی السعادة
lines.en: And the First Teacher, Aristotle, says: The Head of the Dragon with the other planets strengthens them and increases beneficence,

lines.text: ولا یضر القمر لانه ذروته ومع الشمس خاصة یدل علی افراط الضرر و ذهاب البصر لانه بطبیعة
lines.en: and it does not harm the Moon because it is its apogee, and with the Sun especially it indicates excessive harm and loss of sight because it is of the nature

lines.text: النهار و هو منحوس مخالفته پس بنا بر انچه معلم اول فرموده مقارن شمس با راس در دلالت قوی باشد
lines.en: of the day and it is malefic in its opposition. Therefore, based on what the First Teacher has said, the conjunction of the Sun with the Head is strong in indication.

lines.text: (احکام بودن راس با زحل) دلالت کند بر نیکی کشت و زرع و بسیاری گیاهها و میوها

sections.en: On the judgments of the conjunction of the planets

Conjunction of Saturn
with the Head

summary.headline: Head with Saturn: Astrological Judgments
summary.text: Astrological judgments of the planets’ conjunctions with the Moon’s Head and Tail, including differing views on their beneficence and maleficence from astrologers, Indian Brahmins, Sheikh Nizami, and Aristotle. The conjunction of the Head with Saturn is associated with crops, agriculture, buildings, religious institutions, prosperity, social groups, animals, prisoners, shrines, and Khorasan.
